clue.text: This little monkey could lose a quarter to a 12

indicators.note: the monkey's name could shed a quarter and leave a 12, so that quarter is sitting inside the 12's name

parts.note: 12-across is a gnawing animal; the marmot is one
SE, south-east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A small monkey is said to be able to turn into some other creature by losing part of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take SE out of the monkey's name and you are left with MARMOT, a rodent (the answer to 12). So the monkey is MARMOT with SE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a tiny South American primate, a little monkey by any description.

clue.text: It makes the grandee enraged

parts.note: the word 'enraged' is the word 'grandee' with its letters reshuffled; the clue names the device that does that

explanation.surface: Something infuriates a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an insult to a nobleman, but 'enraged' uses exactly the letters of 'grandee'; the thing that turns one into the other is a rearrangement of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one word to spell another is the very device being described.

clue.text: Sensational play barred

parts.note: a sensational play, with 'barred' read as set in musical bars, since the form began as drama with music

explanation.surface: A lurid stage show has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' looks like 'banned', but here it means written in bars of music: the original form was a play with musical accompaniment, later any lurid, sensational drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational, over-emotional stage play with stock villains is the classic form of this genre.

clue.text: Fish from the Psalmist's snow-clad hill

definitions.meaning: a large game fish of rivers and seas
Psalm 68 says the land was 'white as snow in ...', a hill near Shechem

explanation.surface: A fish is taken from a snowy hill named in the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish shares its name with the mountain in Psalm 68 that the Psalmist describes as snowy.

clue.text: Flight of Richard Hannay ?

parts.note: Richard Hannay is John Buchan's hero, who flees across Scotland in his best-known novel; 'flight' is both his escape and a staircase

explanation.surface: A question about the fictional adventurer Richard Hannay running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' reads as Hannay's escape, but it is also a flight of stairs: the title of the 1915 John Buchan thriller in which Hannay goes on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buchan novel, later a Hitchcock film, recounts Hannay's escape, and its title names a staircase.

clue.text: O.K. given by letter or by hand, say ?

parts.note: per is Latin for 'by', as in 'per post'

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the word for hand to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Approval may come in writing or by hand delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Per post' and 'per mitt' are the joke: 'say' makes MITT heard as MIT. 'Given by letter' points to a written authorisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is a written authorisation, an official go-ahead put down on paper.

clue.text: Poets' friend has important store of their treasures

definitions.text: Poets' friend has important store of their treasures

parts.note: pal is an everyday word for a friend
grave means weighty or important

explanation.surface: A friend of poets keeps a significant collection of their best work.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Turner Palgrave compiled 'The Golden Treasury' (1861), the famous anthology of English poems, so the whole clue describes him as well as building his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian anthologist gathered the finest English lyrics into his Golden Treasury, a friend to poets indeed.

clue.text: To finish up in service was Ophelia's' fate

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the church service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for finishing is read bottom to top

parts.note: to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Ending up in religious service was what became of Ophelia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns END into DNE, and 'in' puts it inside MASS. In Hamlet, Ophelia is told 'Get thee to a nunnery', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia in Hamlet goes out of her mind with grief before drowning, so insanity was her lot.

clue.text: Controls for motor-cycles through the races, boy

parts.note: thro' is the old shortened spelling of through
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race meeting
Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: A boy speeds through the races on his motorbike, working the controls.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy, motorcycle road races held on the Isle of Man, which fits the motorbike picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The twist-grip valves that govern engine speed on a motorbike are its main controls.

clue.text: Succumb to the Italian finery

parts.note: to fall is to succumb
al is Italian for 'to the'

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to fancy Italian clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallal is a piece of showy dress ornament, so the word stands for frippery or showy finery.

clue.text: Man's man I defame

parts.note: to slander is to defame

explanation.surface: A man confesses to running someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' with a capital is the Isle of Man, so 'Man's man' is a native of that island, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman is an inhabitant of the Isle of Man, an island dweller.

clue.text: Where Jack finds almost a brand-new wife ?

definitions.text: Where Jack finds almost a brand-new wife ?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for a new wife is dropped

parts.note: a bride is a newly married wife
Jack is a sailor (jack tar), said to have a wife in every port

explanation.surface: A question about where a sailor picks up a newly wed wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A sailor proverbially has a wife in every port. BRIDPORT is a harbour town in Dorset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset harbour town is a place a sailor might put in to, just as the clue describes.

clue.text: Mountainous issue, or a study in nonsense ?

indicators.note: the word for a study goes inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot is nonsense
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A question about what a mountain might produce, or a scholarly study of absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop and Horace, the mountain laboured and brought forth a mouse, so a mountain's offspring is a small gnawing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable, the mountain in labour gives birth only to a mouse, the issue or offspring here.

clue.text: A slur on the slide

definitions.meaning: a damaging, defamatory insinuation about someone
a thin film of a specimen spread on a microscope slide

explanation.surface: An insult delivered as things go downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a defamatory attack and a specimen spread on glass for a microscope go by this word.

clue.text: The sexton's one such as can stir the mixture

indicators.note: a mixture means the letters of 'as can stir' are mixed up

explanation.surface: A church official is the sort who can stir a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture' is the anagram signal for AS CAN STIR. A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building; he is one of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is one kind of church officer who cares for sacred vessels and vestments.

clue.text: Catholic sort of joint

definitions.meaning: with a small c, catholic means wide-ranging, all-embracing
a coupling that lets a shaft turn at an angle, as in a car's drive shaft

explanation.surface: A kind of joint shared by Catholics.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its old sense means all-embracing, and a flexible coupling in engineering bears the same name.

clue.text: Something to remind one about a balance

indicators.note: the word for a memory aid is placed about, or around, the letter A

parts.note: a reminder is something that reminds one

explanation.surface: A memo prompts someone about the state of their bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance is what is left over, as in the rest of a sum after part is paid.

clue.text: He's in a low joint and finds it sticky

indicators.note: the letters of 'He's' are placed inside the word for a seedy bar

parts.note: a dive is a low, disreputable bar or club
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man in a seedy bar finds things tricky there.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'low joint' is a disreputable bar, a DIVE; HES goes inside it, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive as an adjective describes something that clings, like glue.

clue.text: " There's a flower that shall be mine " (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: There's a flower that shall be mine " (Wordsworth)

parts.words: There's a flower that shall be mine " (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the opening of Wordsworth's poem to a small yellow spring flower, whose next line names it

explanation.surface: A line of Wordsworth in which the poet claims a flower as his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's 'To the Small Celandine' runs: 'There's a flower that shall be mine, / 'Tis the little Celandine.' The quotation defines its flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesser celandine is the small yellow spring flower Wordsworth adopts as his own in that poem.

clue.text: Swiss town's cattle fodder

definitions.meaning: a city on its lake in central Switzerland
alfalfa, a clover-like crop grown to feed livestock

explanation.surface: Feed for cows from a town in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Lucerne in Switzerland shares its name with alfalfa, a forage plant fed to cattle.

clue.text: She hasn't scored a hit with Mr. Right? That's wrong!

definitions.text: She hasn't scored a hit with Mr. Right
definitions.meaning: an unmarried woman (a miss) who has not landed a husband, and a shot that fails to hit

explanation.surface: A woman who has not won her ideal man is told she has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A MISS, the answer is both an unmarried woman who has not caught Mr Right and a missed shot; run together it means wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is out of order, faulty or not as it should be.

clue.text: Little sister embraces German gent — gets the sack

indicators.note: the short word for a sister wraps around the German word for a gentleman

parts.note: sis is short for sister
Herr is German for Mr, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A small girl hugs a German man, who then loses his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the sack' suggests dismissal, but sack is an old word for sherry; Falstaff praises 'sherris sack' in Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherris is the old form of sherry, the fortified Spanish wine Elizabethans called sack.

clue.text: Sound advice, should this tap get stuck ?

definitions.text: Sound advice, should this tap get stuck ?

parts.words: Sound advice, should this tap get stuck ?
parts.note: the word, said out loud, is what you would be advised to do to a jammed tap: use some force on it

explanation.surface: Wise counsel for dealing with a stiff tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound advice' means good advice on the surface, but here it means advice heard: the word for a tap, spoken, resembles 'force it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A faucet is a tap, chiefly in American usage, controlling the flow from a pipe.

clue.text: Egg — how nice it is, scrambled

indicators.note: scrambled means the letters of 'nice it' are rearranged, as eggs are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone remarks how lovely scrambled egg is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' is the verb, as in egging someone on, not breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or provoke them into action.

clue.text: With hock in poor condition, hastened to take in a French wine

indicators.note: the word for hastened takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: sped means hastened
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to drink a French wine and suffered a sore leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' tempts as a German wine, but it is a horse's ankle joint; spavin is a swelling of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spavined horse suffers spavin, a disease of the hock joint, leaving it lame or broken-down.

clue.text: The way to act with fish ?

parts.note: a turn is a stage act
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A question about how to perform with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a toll road, a highway or way.

clue.text: Otherwise sacred feature of the Lebanon

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters of 'sacred' are put in another order

explanation.surface: Something sacred is a characteristic of Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: The cedar of Lebanon is the country's emblem and appears on its flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar trees of the Lebanon mountains are famous enough to stand on the national flag.

clue.text: "I've got you under my skin " as the patient might say

definitions.text: "I've got you under my skin " as the patient might say

parts.words: I've got you under my skin " as the patient might say
parts.note: the Cole Porter song line, taken literally as said by someone receiving an injection to the thing piercing them

explanation.surface: A sick person sings a love song line.
explanation.walkthrough: The song line 'I've got you under my skin' is a love declaration, but a patient being injected could say it literally of what has gone in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic is the thin sharp instrument pushed under the skin during an injection.

clue.text: His Juvenalia put one in awkward straits

definitions.text: His Juvenalia put one in awkward straits

indicators.note: the letter for one is put in the rearranged letters
awkward means the letters of 'straits' are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer's early works landed someone in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges STRAITS, and I goes inside. Juvenal was the Roman writer of savage satires, so 'Juvenalia' are satires.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was a Roman mocker of vice, and a writer of such attacks can leave their targets embarrassed.
